scope: Theorem 14.9 (Finite-path transfer) of the manuscript “Virtual compact specialness of hyperbolic one-relator groups” (preprints/Virtual-compact-specialness-of-hyperbolic-one-relator-groups-September-25-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 258 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 a6c45541e6943005), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 102. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Fix an integer n. Under the terminal row hypotheses, there is a finite set of original compatibility requests such that every sufficiently long compatible filling has the following properties. (i) The induced row fillings and edge fillings form the quotient graph of groups for Ḡ. (ii) Every reduced path of length at most n downstairs with infinite stabilizer lifts, after the permitted changes of Bass–Serre representatives, to an actual reduced path upstairs. Its stabilizer is exactly the image of the actual path stabilizer. (iii) Taking n at least the terminal path bound, the resulting Bass–Serre action is acylindrical: sufficiently long segment stabilizers are finite of uniformly bounded order. Each filled row is hyperbolic and each edge map is quasi-isometric. Here the ambient filled group is hyperbolic by sufficiently long filling of the original relatively hyperbolic pair: the periodic peripheral reductions are finite-by-cyclic and hence hyperbolic, and the additional cyclic reductions are finite. The conclusion about ambient quasiconvexity is proved separately below.
